name: Mirumoto Hisa
concept: Hisa's eyes track the doorway long after a student leaves her classroom, following a path only she can see.

answers.giri: Mirumoto Hisa teaches the niten to the War College's advanced students for its commander, Akodo Tsanuri, who has forbidden duels among the College's staff.
answers.ninjo: Hisa wants the duel against a Kakita blade that would settle whether the niten is the lesser style, and Kakita Kensaku, who certifies the armory's steel for the same commander, has never once offered it.
answers.standout_quality: Hisa beats every opponent she faces with the niten except the ones who refuse to let her draw both blades.
answers.accomplishment: She kept three students who had already decided to leave the war college, by teaching them the niten not as a path to glory but as a way to survive what comes after the tournament ends.
answers.challenge: She pitches the niten to every promising student who walks through her classroom door, certain her charm will keep them, and watches them leave anyway because they want a master who will fight the Kakita, not one who teaches them to hide.
answers.peace: Hisa traces the routes between the war college and the villages that surrendered before Snow Plain, marking which paths the students who leave her actually take, mapping their dispersal as carefully as she would chart an unfamiliar coastline.
answers.fear: Hisa teaches in the war college's high tower and refuses assignments that would post her to the garrison towns spreading south from the castle, where ten thousand soldiers crowd the roads and the supply-master's compounds sprawl into villages that have no shape, because she cannot think in a place where everything is built on top of everything else.
answers.accoutrement: A brass compass the size of a thumbnail, worn on a cord under her collar; she checks it each time a student leaves the classroom, marking the direction they went.

clan_relationship.text: Hisa teaches the two-blades form to students who will never face a Kakita, and tells herself this serves the Dragon when what she is really doing is protecting them from a duel she cannot win.

mentor.name: Kumi
mentor.text: Kumi taught her that a wound taken protecting someone else stops hurting differently than one taken for pride, and Hisa has spent fifteen years trying to prove that lesson wrong by pitching the niten to students she believes will stay.

answers.first_impression: Hisa's eyes track the doorway long after a student leaves her classroom, following a path only she can see.
answers.stress_reaction: Hisa stops talking mid-lesson and walks to the window, tracking the student's path down the mountain roads until the figure is too small to follow, and does not resume until someone asks her a direct question.
answers.relationships:
Mirumoto Tsuru (Dragon) — Mirumoto Tsuru left the war college three years ago to join a merchant house that trades south along the coast, and Hisa still calculates which ports the supply ships pass through, cross-referencing them against the seasons.
Ichirō Masu (Badger) — Ichirō Masu of the Badger clan once refused Hisa's offer to teach him the niten, citing his family's traditional forms, and she has spent four years calculating whether his choice was honest principle or polite rejection she failed to charm away.

parent_opinion.description: Hisa's mother wishes she would stop running the war college's classroom like a lighthouse keeping watch for ships that have already sailed past the rocks.

answers.heritage: Ties to the Perfect Land Sect
answers.death: Hisa expects to die in the war college, teaching, with a student she thought had returned finally standing in the doorway.
